name: manual_aff598
claim: SSRF IP-pinning adapters must use the split-identity rule: pool key + TCP target = validated pin (PLACE), TLS SNI/cert + HTTP Host = original hostname (NAME) -- never mutate a shared adapter's connection_pool_kw per-request

decisions.notes: PT #359's original SSRFPinnedHTTPAdapter mutated self.poolmanager.connection_pool_kw per-request (update()/pop()), a real concurrency race: concurrent requests could clobber each other's pin, and stripping pinned_ip from the custom PoolKey normalizer (to avoid a PoolKey.__new__() crash) let two different validated IPs for the same hostname share one pool -- cross-contamination on reuse. Fix: override HTTPAdapter.build_connection_pool_key_attributes() and set host_params['host']=pinned_ip -- urllib3's stock PoolKey (keyed on scheme/host/port) becomes naturally pin-aware with zero custom fields. Converged independently across 3 sources (own research, Agnes's Reference Guide 09, Perplexity's review 09b) -- see references/09-SSRF-IP-PINNING-CONCURRENCY-AND-POOLMANAGER-CONVERGENCE-2026-08-22.md and 09b-Perplexity-review.md. Landed as PT commits 351bad1e + 5a6a4ae7 (2026-08-22/23).
